question: Is betaN from the map's own current (Grad-Shafranov split of J_phi into p' and FF' on the solve's three terms, equilibrium_beta.py) a better label-free MAST betaN than the kinetic estimate (Thomson p_e x 2.25)?
rule_3: DIII-D labels only; no MAST label/demo/leaderboard number.
seen_before_freezing: smoke on 2 validation shots (38 frames) printed: sum J dA = Ip within ~2 % in flat-top (units OK); eq/label ~0.75 on one shot and ~2 on the other, pressure share ~0.37 nearly constant; kinetic closer on both. Disclosed; the formal test uses the same 60 shots as M1b.
data: as M1b: DIII-D validation bucket, first 60 sorted shots, every 4th frame, |Ip| >= 0.3 MA, true maps; axis/LCFS/axis-flux handling as M1b amendment 1.
metrics: R2 on frames finite in both arms, median ratio, bias-removed R2, correlation, finite share.
decision_rule: Equilibrium betaN is a MAST candidate only if its R2 >= the kinetic R2 AND its bias-removed R2 >= the kinetic bias-removed R2 on true DIII-D maps. Otherwise it is recorded as rejected and MAST keeps the kinetic estimate.
